note: Ceilings in gzip bytes, written by "node budget.mjs --update" with 10% headroom.
sharedGzip is the payload every page declares: webpack runtime, main bundle, stylesheet.
chunkGzip caps any single route chunk, so one heavy page cannot hide behind an average.
Raise a ceiling deliberately and say why in the commit. Do not raise it to make CI pass.
chunkGzip was 189 kB while Mermaid shipped a 171 kB chunk. Mermaid was removed on
2026-08-23 and the largest route chunk is now 17.6 kB, so that ceiling had stopped
meaning anything. Set to 64 kB by hand rather than measured+10%: tight enough to catch a
dependency of that size arriving again, loose enough for a genuinely heavy interactive
page. If a real page needs more, raise it in the same commit that adds the page.
onDemandGzip, added 2026-08-25 with the documentation assistant.
An on-demand chunk is one no route fetches: it arrives only when a reader opens the panel.
Membership comes from results/on-demand-chunks.json, written by "npm run chunk-cost", which
loads real routes in a browser, records every script fetched on load, then opens the assistant
and records what arrives only after. Measured, not inferred, because webpack names most chunks
by content hash and a static allowlist cannot cover them. It fails closed: an unlisted chunk is
held to the tighter chunkGzip ceiling, so a stale list produces a failure, never a false pass.
onDemandChunks below is for explicitly named chunks and is a second, optional source.
Measured 2026-08-25: opening the panel costs 151.6 kB across three chunks, and no assistant
chunk is fetched on any route load. Almost all of it is the micromark/remark/rehype markdown
pipeline plus marked, needed to render a streaming answer without the code-fence flicker a
naive renderer produces.
Set to 160 kB by hand: close to the measurement, so it leaves room for ordinary churn and none
for a second heavy dependency arriving unnoticed. If the panel needs more, reduce it instead.
The documented fallback is react-markdown plus remend with hand-rolled block splitting.
Re-measured 2026-08-25 after the entry points changed: opening the panel costs 151.2 kB across
two chunks, and shared first-load fell from 191.7 to 172.6 kB because shadowing @theme/SearchBar
moved the search theme's runtime and Comlink out of the main bundle into the on-demand ask modal
chunk. Ceilings left where they were: the headroom is the point, not a target to spend.
Everything is measured per locale from 2026-08-27, and each ceiling gates the worst locale. A
localised build is a whole site per locale, so measuring the tree as one site counted the two
font files six times and intersected English HTML with Russian HTML, which named main.js at a
different path and emptied the shared set. sharedGzip then measured nothing while all three main
bundles were held against the per-route-chunk ceiling. Reasoning is in budget.mjs.
sharedGzip raised from 192 to 200 kB on 2026-08-27, deliberately. A locale compiles its own
translation catalogue into main.js, so the Russian bundle is 156.9 kB against the English
151.8 kB, and Russian shared first-load measures 195.8 kB against 190.7. The old ceiling was set
while the site was English-only and no longer covered the largest language it ships. 200 kB, not
measured+10%, which would have been 215 kB: 4 kB of headroom is enough for catalogue churn and
not enough to hide a dependency. Adding a locale does not push this up, since each locale is
measured on its own; a verbose new language could, and then the number moves again with a reason.
